title: Network organization of protein binding-site landscapes across scales
summary: ProtT5-based network analysis identifies multiscale organization and cross-protein recognition relationships among experimentally resolved binding sites; drug cross-reactivity remains a hypothesis.
ai_technology: ProtT5 protein-language-model embeddings and binding-site network analysis
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Results, “Structural calibration and a nonredundant binding site atlas” and “Local network neighborhoods”: 121,673-node network, ligand-class assortativity 0.72; communities resolve kinase-site environments and local relationships across low-sequence-identity proteins
evidence.unknown: Results: embedding proximity associated with local ProBiS structural similarity; source is experimentally resolved BioLiP2/PDB sites. Source discussion limits pharmacological implications to hypotheses requiring follow-up
evidence.ai_role: Materials and Methods, “Binding site embeddings and network construction”: ProtT5 residue vectors averaged into 1,024 dimensions, then mutual k-nearest-neighbor network analysis

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
